# Canva Resume Templates Guide

Overview of resume template categories and how to choose the right one for your needs.

## Template Categories

### 1. Modern Minimalist

**Characteristics**:
- Clean lines and whitespace
- Sans-serif fonts (Montserrat, Lato, Open Sans)
- Subtle colors or black & white
- Simple dividers and elements
- Professional but contemporary look

**Best for**: Tech, Startups, Design, Modern companies

**Features**:
- Single or two-column layout
- Emphasis on readability
- Minimal decoration
- ATS-friendly

**When to use**:
- Applying to tech companies
- Digital-first roles
- Creative positions
- Modern brand culture

---

### 2. Classic Professional

**Characteristics**:
- Traditional layout
- Serif fonts (Garamond, Times, Merriweather)
- Neutral colors (navy, gray, black)
- Formal structure
- Timeless appeal

**Best for**: Finance, Law, Consulting, Government

**Features**:
- Balanced layout
- Professional typography
- Traditional sections
- Highly readable

**When to use**:
- Conservative industries
- Executive roles
- Corporate positions
- Traditional hiring processes

---

### 3. Creative/Designer

**Characteristics**:
- Unique visual elements
- Bold colors or patterns
- Creative typography
- Portfolio or showcase elements
- Unconventional layout

**Best for**: Designers, Creatives, Artists, Marketing roles

**Features**:
- Visual emphasis
- Custom graphics
- Artistic fonts
- Eye-catching design

**When to use**:
- Design or creative roles
- Portfolio-focused positions
- Companies valuing creativity
- Visual-first industries

---

### 4. Two-Column Layout

**Characteristics**:
- Left column for contact/skills/about
- Right column for experience/education
- Efficient use of space
- Often more content fits

**Best for**: Experienced professionals, multiple achievements

**Features**:
- Compact design
- Organized sections
- More room for details
- Can feel cramped if not spaced well

**When to use**:
- 5+ years of experience
- Multiple projects or certifications
- Technical roles with many skills
- Need to fit lots of information

---

### 5. Single Column Layout

**Characteristics**:
- Vertical flow top to bottom
- Traditional left-to-right reading
- Clean, straightforward design
- Easiest to read on mobile

**Best for**: Most industries, ATS-friendly approach

**Features**:
- Simple structure
- Easy to follow
- Mobile-friendly
- Most ATS-compatible

**When to use**:
- First-time job seekers
- ATS submission required
- Most traditional applications
- Reading ease priority

---

### 6. Infographic/Visual

**Characteristics**:
- Charts or visual representations
- Skill bars or rating graphics
- Timeline elements
- Visual storytelling

**Best for**: Creative industries, portfolios, visual roles

**Features**:
- Eye-catching elements
- Visual skill representation
- Unique design
- May not be ATS-friendly

**Caution**: Many online job portals can't parse visual elements, so have a text-based version ready

---

## Choosing the Right Template

### Decision Tree

**Question 1: Industry/Field?**
- Tech/Startup → Modern Minimalist
- Finance/Law/Corporate → Classic Professional
- Design/Creative → Creative/Designer
- Traditional → Classic Professional

**Question 2: Years of Experience?**
- 0-2 years → Single Column or Two-Column (simple)
- 2-5 years → Two-Column or Modern Minimalist
- 5+ years → Two-Column with more space

**Question 3: Submission Method?**
- Online portal → Single Column (ATS-friendly)
- Email/Direct → Any template
- PDF viewed on screen → Two-Column or Modern Minimalist
- Printed copies → Classic Professional

**Question 4: Priority?**
- Readability → Single Column
- Modern appearance → Modern Minimalist
- Creativity/Uniqueness → Creative/Designer
- Professionalism → Classic Professional

## Customization Tips

### After Choosing a Template

1. **Color Customization**
   - Replace default colors with your brand palette
   - Maintain contrast and readability
   - Use consistent color throughout
   - Test black & white printing

2. **Font Adjustment**
   - Keep heading font different from body font
   - Ensure all fonts are readable at small sizes
   - Match template style with font choice
   - Don't use more than 2-3 fonts

3. **Content Replacement**
   - Replace dummy text with your information
   - Maintain formatting and spacing
   - Keep bullet point style consistent
   - Verify all dates and details

4. **Layout Tweaking**
   - Adjust spacing between sections as needed
   - Add/remove sections based on your needs
   - Ensure single-page format
   - Check alignment and symmetry

---

## Template Variations

### Role-Specific Variations

You can modify a single template for different roles:

**Base Template**: Modern Minimalist

**Variations**:
- **Tech Role Version**: Emphasize technical skills, projects
- **Sales Role Version**: Highlight achievements, metrics
- **Marketing Role Version**: Add creative projects, campaigns
- **Leadership Version**: Emphasize team size, scope, impact

---

## ATS Compatibility by Template Type

| Template Type | ATS Friendly | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Single Column | ✓✓✓ Excellent | Best for parsing |
| Two Column | ✓✓ Good | Usually ok, some parsing issues |
| Classic Professional | ✓✓✓ Excellent | Standard format works well |
| Modern Minimalist | ✓✓ Good | Clean lines work ok |
| Creative/Designer | ✗✗ Poor | Visual elements confuse parsers |
| Infographic/Visual | ✗✗✗ Very Poor | Can't parse graphics |

**Safe bet**: Use single-column or classic professional for ATS submissions

---

## Template Selection Checklist

- [ ] Template matches your industry style
- [ ] Fits your years of experience
- [ ] ATS-friendly if needed
- [ ] Can be customized to your colors/fonts
- [ ] Fits one page with your content
- [ ] Easy to read on mobile
- [ ] Looks good in print (if needed)
- [ ] Matches your personal brand
- [ ] Professional appearance
- [ ] All sections you need are included

---

## After Selecting & Customizing

**Final steps**:
1. Review [Design Checklist](./design-checklist.md) for quality
2. Proofread for errors
3. Check in [Colors & Fonts](./colors-fonts.md) for guidance
4. Export using [Export Guide](./export.md)
5. Save multiple versions if role-specific

**Before sending**:
1. Print preview or PDF preview
2. Check on multiple devices (computer, tablet, phone)
3. Have someone else review
4. Verify all information is current and correct
